**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-open-science.html#/part-2-the-claim-and-its-estimand){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).

Part 2 reads the paper in full, then argues that analysts who look as though they disagree are often answering different questions, and gives you the estimand statement as the way of saying which question you are answering. It ends with the five Task 2 analyses read as five questions, which is where the choice of Part 3 comes from. The part takes ninety minutes.

## 1. The paper

**On the slides.** The slides present the paper of the original author (OA): the claim as the analysts received it, the four framing scales, the model that the OA fitted, and Model 1 and Model 2, which put the robustness question inside the paper. The slides go on to the data of the OA against the panel of the course, the attempts to reproduce the paper, the replication on new data and the three Rs on this paper. The run ends on the five questions that the Multi100 analysts asked in the free phase of the project.

## 2. Estimands

**On the slides.** Two studies are set beside our five. The red-card estimates return as a single row, with four estimands drawn out of one football question and the spread that collapses once the estimand is fixed. The slides then ask what research questions that leave the estimand open mean for the reading of many-analysts studies, and present the three steps from a theoretical to an empirical estimand that Lundberg and colleagues set out.

## 3. The estimand statement

**On the slides.** The slides give the template of the estimand statement for the claim of the day. You write a statement of one sentence in the chat, hold it, and send it with the rest of the class when the facilitator says go. The slides then set the five Task 2 analyses side by side, each with its unit, outcome, series and comparison, as five answers to five questions.

## 4. Task 2 – The panel and the estimand statement

[Open the browser lab at Task 2](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-2-get-the-data-and-look-at-it){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Look at the panel and find the countries that move sharply around 2009. Then write your estimand statement properly, with the [template](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-estimand-and-dag) further down the task. The causal graph below the template is optional today. If you work in the workspace, use the working script or your report instead.

**By the end of the part** you have an estimand statement for the claim in your notes, and you can say which question each of the five analysts answered.
